title: Cambodia
capsule: Between 1700 and 1803, the post-Angkorian Khmer kingdom ruled from the Oudong capital was caught in an escalating contest between Siam and the Nguyen lords of Vietnam for control of the Mekong basin. Cambodian kings such as Ang Tong and Ang Non were repeatedly installed and deposed through Siamese or Vietnamese intervention, and in 1794 the Siamese extracted the provinces of Battambang and Siem Reap, home to the ruins of Angkor, as the price of restoring a Siamese-backed prince to the throne. The era closed as Ang Chan II acceded around 1802-1806 and accepted simultaneous tributary status to both the newly unified Nguyen Vietnam of Emperor Gia Long and to Siam, cementing Cambodia's dual-vassal position for the following decades.
